title: Thin-film LN modulator
title_note: Accelerated preview read for this story; the version of record (published online 2018-09-24, Nature 562, 101-104) has the same abstract and the same captions of Extended Data Fig. 1, 3, 4 and 5; its main text and Methods were not compared. No separate Supplementary Information: Methods and Extended Data only. The electrodes are drawn as a later differential T-rail design by other groups (T-segment geometry from Kharel et al., Optica 2021; S̅ S S̅ drive from Aimone et al., OFC 2026); the 2018 device used plain ground-signal-ground electrodes with a single drive, and the plots show the 2018 device's measured results.

parts.name: Inverted-signal strips (S̅)
parts.role: Outer strips carrying the inverted signal (later differential drive); in 2018 these were grounds
parts.detail: Drawn as a later design: Aimone et al. (OFC 2026) drive a standard three-conductor travelling-wave electrode, 7.5 mm long, 50 Ω, periodically capacitively loaded (segment sizes not printed), with integrated NiCr terminations, on 350 nm LN on silicon. A SiGe driver delivers S̅ S S S̅ to four input pads: the two inner pads feed the centre strip, the outer pads the two outer strips, with no ground between the signal electrodes. The gap voltage doubles compared with a single-ended drive while the two arms still see opposite fields (push-pull). Later work, not the 2018 device: Wang et al. 2018 used ground strips (G) of a plain ground-signal-ground line with a single drive; "The optical waveguides run through the dielectric gaps of a ground–signal–ground coplanar microwave strip line (Fig. 1d)" (p.1). 2018 device: gap about 4.5 µm (read from the simulation cross-section of Extended Data Fig. 5c, d; consistent with the stated metal-to-waveguide spacing <2.5 µm), ground width not printed. Drawn: body 150 µm wide (assumed) with T segments on the inner edge (Kharel et al. geometry).

parts.name: T-rail segments
parts.role: T-shaped segments along every gap edge (later design); current flows in the wide bodies
parts.detail: Kharel et al. (Optica 2021) replaced plain coplanar strips with T-rail ("micro-structured") electrodes: channel bodies like a coplanar line plus T segments reaching toward the waveguide. The segments keep the current out of the narrow gap and spread it in the wide body, so the ohmic loss drops without widening the gap; they add capacitance and slow the microwave. Kharel et al. built them on LN on quartz (600 nm film, 350 nm etch, 0.8 µm gold) and measured 2 dB/cm at 50 GHz against 7 dB/cm for regular electrodes on LN on silicon. Aimone et al. (OFC 2026) used periodically loaded electrodes on LN on silicon but print no segment sizes. This drawing applies Kharel's segment geometry to the 2018 stack (silicon, 4.7 µm oxide, 600 nm film), 1.1 µm gold kept from 2018; velocity matching of this combination is not claimed (Kharel et al.: on LN on silicon with a thick oxide the slow-wave effect of the segments is undesirable, hence their quartz handle, p.3). Facing rows mirror-aligned, one stem centred on each cap. Close-ups are true size (period 50 µm); in the whole-chip view the segment count is illustrative (the true 400 periods along 20 mm would alias on the shortened plan). Later work, not the 2018 device.
parts.quote: The segments prevent electrical current from flowing in the closest gap region, while allowing the current to be distributed more uniformly in the wide channel region.
parts.locator: Kharel et al., Optica 2021 (arXiv v1, 2020), p.3, Sec. II

parts.name: Microwave field
parts.role: Field across the gaps, opposite in sign in the two arms; arrows illustrative (simulation figure)
parts.detail: "The microwave electric field has opposite signs across the two LN waveguides, thus inducing (through the Pockels effect) an optical phase delay on one arm and an optical phase advance on the other." Extended Data Fig. 5c shows the simulated field (E_{z}) in one gap for 1 V across the electrodes; its colour scale runs from 0 to about 4 × 10^{5} V/m. Rendered as an effect (arrows along ±z in the two gaps), not a body. The arrows are drawn above the ridge for visibility; the simulated field also crosses the ridge and slab (Extended Data Fig. 5c). In the true-size close-ups the field is drawn at an illustrative 34 GHz: its wavelength (c / (2.2 f) = 4 mm, from the stated group index 2.2) spans about 80 segment periods, far longer than the view, so the field there is nearly uniform and oscillates in time. The travelling wave is shown only in the whole-chip view, where the wavelength is drawn about 20x shortened, like the plan. In the bandwidth chapter the drive frequency and the modulation depth follow the 20 mm response (Fig. 2a) and hold where that trace ends (about 43 GHz); the 10 mm and 5 mm curves are other, shorter devices. No microwave loss is drawn along the line (not printed). Drawn drive: differential (later design, Aimone et al.): the centre strip and the outer strips swing in antiphase (amber positive, blue negative on the strips), so the field in the two gaps stays opposite; the 2018 device was driven single-ended on a ground-signal-ground line. The velocity matching shown is the 2018 plain ground-signal-ground line's: T segments add capacitance and slow the microwave; Kharel et al. note that on LN on silicon with a thick oxide this slow-wave effect is undesirable and used a quartz handle (Optica 2021, arXiv v1, p.3). Matching of the drawn T-rail line on the 2018 stack is not claimed.

parts.name: Mach-Zehnder modulator
parts.role: Travelling-wave push-pull Mach-Zehnder interferometer, 20 mm electrodes
parts.detail: Travelling-wave Mach-Zehnder interferometer: microwave and light co-propagate with matched group velocities (both about 2.2). Half-wave voltage 1.4 V for the 20 mm device (Vπ·L 2.8 V·cm, Extended Data Table 1); 2.3 V and 4.4 V for the 10 mm and 5 mm devices (2.3 and 2.2 V·cm). Vπ was measured with a 5 V peak-to-peak triangular drive. The plan view is drawn shortened about 20x along the device (layout of the 20 mm chip withheld); widths and the cross-section are to scale. The electrodes are drawn as a later differential T-rail design (Kharel et al. 2021 geometry, Aimone et al. 2026 drive); the 2018 device used plain ground-signal-ground electrodes with a single drive, and every value here is the 2018 device's.

chapters.action: finished chip floats in, tilted, light running through the Mach-Zehnder; slow drift

chapters.line: Lithium niobate film on buried oxide on silicon.
chapters.action: camera dives to a cut through the electrode section; the chip dissolves to the bare silicon; buried SiO2 and the 600 nm LN film settle on it (cross-section to scale)

chapters.line: Half the film is etched away, leaving two ridges.
chapters.action: macro on the left arm; the top 300 nm outside the ridge etches down to the slab; pull back to show both ridges

chapters.line: Later design: T segments reach from three gold strips into each gap.
chapters.action: later design (labelled): the three strips S̅, S, S̅ land on the slab together (one gold lift-off), then the camera moves to a top-down close-up of one gap and rows of T segments grow from the strip edges into it (true size: caps 45 µm, period 50 µm, 5 µm between facing caps); the ridge sits centred in the gap

chapters.line: Silica deposited over the whole chip.
chapters.action: flat-topped translucent oxide settles from above (as the schematics draw it), then turns faint so the stack stays readable

chapters.line: One arm per gap, split and recombined by Y-junctions.
chapters.action: camera pulls back to the whole chip (length compressed): input Y, two arms in the gaps, output Y; light enters, splits and recombines; driver pads (S̅ S S S̅) and one load per conductor at the ends of the line

chapters.line: Later design: outer strips carry the inverted signal; fields oppose.
chapters.action: true-size close-up (later design): differential drive, centre strip and outer strips in antiphase, field arrows across both gaps in opposite directions, mode spot under each ridge; the field is drawn at an illustrative 34 GHz with its true 4 mm wavelength, so it is nearly uniform over the view and flips in time (three cycles), first on the face, then looking down the line; it fades before the pull-back. The travelling wave with the co-moving light is shown only in the whole-chip view (bandwidth chapter, wavelength shortened like the plan)

chapters.line: Swing from bright to dark with CMOS-level voltage.
chapters.action: model left half (whole chip); plots.transfer assembles; the drive sweeps 0 to 2.8 V with the plot and the output brightness follows the digitized transfer curve

chapters.line: Slow roll-off to tens of gigahertz; shorter devices go faster.
chapters.action: plots.eo_20mm assembles (alternates 10 mm, 5 mm on the same 0-100 GHz axis); model left half; the drive frequency follows the pen of the 20 mm trace and holds where the trace ends (about 43 GHz); the microwave on the strip shortens in wavelength (c / (2.2 f)), light rides with it; output modulation depth 0.7 times the amplitude ratio of S21 from the same trace; no microwave loss drawn

chapters.line: More bandwidth per volt than earlier lithium niobate modulators.
chapters.action: plots.fom assembles; model holds the last bandwidth state (end of the 20 mm trace, its depth), left half; orbit and explode offered

withheld.what: Signal and ground line widths of the 20 mm device
withheld.reason: Not printed; the Methods say only that the signal line width was designed with the oxide thickness for velocity matching and about 50 Ω. Rendered widths are assumed (the Fig. 1d test chip shows about 40-56 and 80-100 µm signal lines by the scale bar; strip edges not resolved).

withheld.what: Electrode gap as a stated value
withheld.reason: Not printed. About 4.5 µm is read from the simulation cross-section (Extended Data Fig. 5c, d) with the stated 300 nm slab as scale; consistent with the stated metal-to-waveguide spacing <2.5 µm. Shown with basis digitized.

withheld.what: Plan layout of the 20 mm device (arm spacing, Y-junction length and angle, bends, chip size, pad layout)
withheld.reason: No drawing of the 20 mm chip. The Fig. 1d micrograph shows a chip with shorter devices (electrodes about 5.0, 4.9 and 3.2 mm by its 500 µm scale bar; an on-chip label reads "Length 0.5 cm Width 700 nm"), so it cannot be scaled to the 20 mm device. The plan view is schematic and its length compressed.

withheld.what: Ridge sidewall angle as a stated value
withheld.reason: Not in the text; about 74 deg from the film plane is read from the simulation drawing (Extended Data Fig. 5d) only.

Methods give only "800-nm-thick SiO_{2} layer by plasma-enhanced chemical vapour deposition"; the 1.1 µm electrodes are thicker than the coat; schematics draw a flat oxide. Rendered translucent and flat-topped as the schematics; top height and profile assumed.

withheld.what: Measured propagation loss of the 800 nm waveguides on this chip
withheld.reason: The Methods quote about 0.2 dB/cm for this width in relation to the group's earlier loss study (ref. 28); it is not presented as a measurement on these devices. The measured statement for this chip is the on-chip loss upper bound <0.5 dB.

The this-work losses in Extended Data Table 1 (0.4, 0.2, 0.1 dB) and the markers in Fig. 4d (about 0.6, 0.3, 0.15 dB) differ, and both scale with electrode length from a per-length loss tied to the earlier study; not plotted.
Density images; only BER values, drive voltages and rates are stated (used in the data plot). No eye is redrawn.

withheld.what: BER versus OSNR (Extended Data Fig. 4) and the 10 mm / 5 mm transfer curves (Extended Data Fig. 1b, c)
withheld.reason: Not digitized for this story (raster figures; values not needed for the chapters).

withheld.what: Microwave loss, characteristic impedance value and microwave index other than about 2.2
withheld.reason: Not printed (impedance "near 50 Ω", group indices "both approximately 2.2").
GGB probes, tapered lensed fibres and the measurement set-up are named but not drawn; ends are shown as neutral markers and light beams only.
Extended Data Fig. 5c, d are simulations (COMSOL, E_{z}); the optical mode has no printed scale. Field arrows and the mode spot are illustrative.
Data tests bias the modulator at the transmission null; how the bias is applied is not described.

withheld.what: The 2018 electrode layout as drawn geometry
withheld.reason: Owner decision: the drawing shows a later differential T-rail design (Kharel et al. 2021 segment geometry, Aimone et al. 2026 S̅ S S̅ drive) instead of the 2018 plain ground-signal-ground line. The 2018 gap (about 4.5 µm, digitized) and widths stay in the part details as 2018 values; all plots are the 2018 device.

withheld.what: GSSG or G-S-G-S-G electrode drawn as the differential drive
withheld.reason: Not drawn. A plain GSSG with one arm in each outer gap gives the same phase shift in both arms on x-cut LN (US 12,619,109 B2, FIG. 1C), so push-pull is lost; Aimone et al. (p.1) state that GS̅GSG and GS̅SG "are not inherently compatible" with the three-conductor electrode. The S̅ S S̅ scheme is shown because its conductor roles are printed. No ground is drawn between the two signals.

withheld.what: Segment dimensions and cross-section of the differential-drive device
withheld.reason: Aimone et al. state periodic capacitive loading on 350 nm LN on silicon but print no segment, gap, width, oxide, etch or metal values; the drawing uses Kharel et al. segment sizes on the 2018 stack, labelled.

withheld.what: Number of segments along the 20 mm line
withheld.reason: Not stated; true size (period 50 µm) in the close-ups, an illustrative count in the shortened whole-chip view.

withheld.what: Field and current distribution around the T segments
withheld.reason: Kharel et al. Fig. 1(c, d) are artistic views; no simulated field map is printed. Field arrows across the cap gap are illustrative.
Chen et al. (Laser Photonics Rev. 2025) claim the first differential-drive push-pull modulator on thin-film LN; Aimone et al. cite an earlier conference paper not found. No "first" is shown.
